prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, and the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B050 as my preferred prize, unchanged in configuration from round 1, and the exchange has made me more confident in it rather than less. The scientific core is a sharp prediction and a decisive measurement: Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 classification and showed that spin-orbit coupling can give a time-reversal-protected insulator with conducting edge channels, and Molenkamp's HgTe quantum-well experiment measured the quantised edge conductance that the prediction demands. It is independently confirmed in transport and ARPES across several material families after about two decades, so neither maturity nor reproducibility is in question, and no one in round 1 argued that the physics fails. What round 1 did was sharpen the wording. Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson have persuaded me that the citation should anchor on the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect, which is where Kane, Mele and Molenkamp are the three people with the central roles, and should say plainly what is new relative to 2016. I therefore adopt Danielsson's and Eriksson's wording of the experimental half, naming HgTe quantum wells, because that is the claim the evidence supports and it avoids implying credit for the three-dimensional work or for later materials screening. I am holding to this on scientific grounds, and the four-member lean toward B050 in the chair summary is not my reason. The chair's summary itself notes that those four positions are stated preferences, not hidden votes.
statement.case_against: The real defect is attribution, and I will not call it clean. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe proposal that told Molenkamp where to look, and the three-dimensional contributors (Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan) are outside the credited names. Under a three-laureate limit I cannot find a principled way to place all of them, and substituting BHZ for Mele or Molenkamp would damage either the originating theory or the experimental half. The second risk is the 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions, which a critic will call the same territory. My answer is that 2016 concerned topological phase transitions and quantum-Hall-type topology, whereas a time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulator with no net magnetic field is a separate, symmetry-protected achievement, but that is a judgement the committee has to own in the citation. If a majority concluded that the BHZ omission makes the experimental half indefensible, I would turn to B051, whose two-name credit is the cleanest on the shortlist.

responses.point: Kroll, answering the chair's question about criteria, states that B050 opened a new conceptual organising principle while the lattice clock opened a new level of accuracy, and that the committee must decide which it rates higher. He also argues that the magic-wavelength condition makes the clock different in principle from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion work and that the redefinition of the second should not delay a prize.
responses.response: I accept his argument that the lattice clock is a distinct principle and not merely a refinement, and I accept that the SI redefinition should not govern the timing; I said in round 1 that if the committee wants to wait it must decide so explicitly, and I see no scientific reason to wait. That is why B051 stays as my first alternative. Where I differ is on how to rank them this year. The clock credit is cleaner, but I read the criterion as favouring the achievement in which a theoretical prediction was tested by an experiment and opened a new field, and B050 fits that better than a metrological advance whose reach is mainly through measurement. I also hold that lattice clocks lean on Ye's accuracy record, which is a continuing programme that will still be there for a later committee. I would accept B051 without objection if the credit question on B050 is judged unsolvable.

responses.point: Danielsson says the 2D quantum spin Hall effect carries the central credit, that the 3D generalisation is a separate achievement to be kept out of the citation, that the BHZ omission cannot be waved away but could be accepted if recorded openly, and that a theory-only Kane-Mele prize would lose the confirmation that makes the case.
responses.response: I agree with each of those points and have adopted his anchoring in my citation. I want to add the experimentalist's reason for keeping Molenkamp: the HgTe conductance measurement is what turned the Z2 prediction into an observed state of matter, and it is the part of the case that the committee can verify against a measured quantity. A theory-only prize would honour the idea but would drop that test. I also accept his demand that the BHZ choice be recorded openly instead of called clean, and my case_against does that. I would still press him on one point: if he accepts the supplied names under the ceiling, he should say whether he would withdraw support if a colleague showed that BHZ rather than Molenkamp is the better third name, because that is the only substitution I can see that would change my own position.

responses.point: Olsson asks whether the 2D effect or 3D topological insulators should anchor B050, says Kane and Mele supplied a time-reversal-invariant state that the 2016 work did not anticipate, and rejects a theory-only prize because the HgTe observation made the prediction a discovery.
responses.response: I agree with her rejection of a theory-only prize and with her request that the citation state the distinction from 2016. My citation names the quantum spin Hall effect and the HgTe observation specifically, so the 3D materials remain outside it, which also keeps within the three credited names. I would resist the alternative reading that 3D topological insulators had the larger impact and so should anchor the prize: the larger impact came from work by names we have not been supplied, and anchoring on it would force a different three-person configuration with a weaker experimental link. Her own caveat that Molenkamp's role depends on the earlier BHZ proposal is correct, and I do not think the citation can hide it.

responses.point: Johansson ranks trapped-ion computing (Cirac, Zoller, Blatt) first, argues that the Wineland overlap is answered because this would honour a computational architecture, and calls B050 a credible alternative he would not block, though the BHZ omission means a decisive theory contribution is missing.
responses.response: I take the architecture argument seriously and I list B015 as a second alternative for that reason. My reservations are the ones he states himself and I weigh them more heavily than he does. The experimental slot between Blatt, Wineland and Monroe is partly arbitrary, and Cirac and Zoller are also the theory originators in B027, so a choice for B015 spends the same recognition as a choice for B027. I also consider the prediction-then-measurement structure of B050 closer to what a prize recognises than a computing architecture whose scalable form has not been demonstrated. I do not agree that the BHZ omission is decisive against B050 while the choice of Blatt over Wineland does not hurt B015; both carry a credit problem of similar size, but the HgTe experiment has no earlier prize behind it, whereas the 2012 prize already covers much of the ion-control experimental work.

uncertainties: Whether the BHZ omission and the exclusion of the 3D contributors can be defended under a three-laureate limit, or whether the committee will judge the experimental credit untenable.
Whether the Academy will treat the Z2 and quantum spin Hall achievement as distinct from the 2016 topological-phases prize, which depends on how the citation is worded.
Whether the committee should weight a new organising principle with complicated credit (B050) above a metrological advance with the cleanest credit on the shortlist (B051).

I replaced B002 with B015 as a second alternative because B002 is still young and the mechanism of its superconductivity is unsettled; that choice rests on my reading of round 1 and I have not verified priority details myself.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B050, B051 or B015. My documented connections (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur, KTH astroparticle group) are in astroparticle instrumentation and do not touch any credited name on these entries; I have no field proximity to any of them beyond a general experimentalist's interest in detector-based measurement. I also chair the committee in this simulation and have no recusal to disclose. I note Johansson's recusal from B038 and Kroll's disclosed proximity to B051 and B015, neither of which affects the entry I propose.
